newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia seen boosting health fund surcharge.
newsitem.headline: Australia seen boosting health fund surcharge.

text.p: Australia's government planned to sharply increase a tax surcharge for healthcare levied on high income earners, The Australian newspaper said on Tuesday.
The increased Medicare surcharge would be announced next month in the budget for the 1997/98 year ending June 30, the paper said, citing unnamed government sources.
The Australian said the surcharge, originally planned at one percent, would be increased "sharply", but did not give a figure.
The Liberal-National government announced the surcharge, to take effect from July, in its 1996/97 budget.

The extra payment was aimed at encouraging high income earners to pay for private health insurance instead of the national public health scheme, Medicare, which is partly funded by an additional levy on income tax.
The Medicare surcharge would apply to individuals earning more than A$50,000 and couples earning more than A$100,000.
Government officials were not immediately available for comment.
Treasurer Peter Costello is due to release the budget for the fiscal year to June 30, 1998, on May 13.
